the observed baryon asymetry of the Universe can be generated in the framework of supersymmetric type-I seesaw leptogenesis, with four zero textures of the neutrino Yukawas, provided that the light neutrino mass spectrum is inverted and the lightest of the three singlet neutrino masses is in the range 10^8 - 10^9 GeV.

(a) the observed value of η is compatible with the model, provided that the CP phases are large and (b) the model is predictive, as the number of free parameters can be reduced to three, namely two Majorana phases and a single Yukawa coupling.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, with the assumption of four zeroes in Yν, the observed value of the baryon asym- metry can be generated in the framework of type-I seesaw leptogenesis, with the light neutrino mass spectrum of normal ordering, and the CP-violating phase δCP in the range 0 < δCP < π/2.

, in the case of four-zero textures for Yν, the observed baryon asym-etry is realized with the help of a single CP-violating phase, and the heavy Majorana neutrino masses are restricted to a relatively narrow range, Mi ~ O(1013) GeV, for a given value of tan β.
, with the assumption of μτ symmetry, the generation of the right baryon asymmetries η in the Universe from supersymetric leptogenesis with the four zero neutrino Yν textures is quite robust.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the observed baryon asymmetries can be obtained in the presence of four zero textures of the neutrino Yukawas, with the light neutrino mass spectrum being either normal or inverted, and in a large portion of the parameter space, the baryon asymetry is obtained for a single sign of the CP violating phase of the Dirac neutrino mass matrix.

the baryon asymetry of the Universe can be generated by a single phase, with the help of a single heavy Majorana neutrino, and with a single nonvanishing CP violating phase in the neutrino sector, provided that this phase is large enough.
, in spite of the severe constraints on the model parameters, it is possible to generate the observed baryon asymetry in a large region of the parameter space.
